messages:
maya: FYI major customer escalations — three different customers reporting truncated/partial SSE streams when their client reconnects after an auth refresh (401 -> refresh -> reconnect). All using TS SDK or raw EventSource. Repro steps and logs below.

sam: Which customers? are they on dedicated or hosted? any shared model/region?

maya: Customers A and B on hosted (us-west1), C on Dedicated pool-03. All using the same model family (open-llama-70b-ish). Not traffic spike related. Latency fine until the reconnect.

maya: Observed behaviour: client gets partial tokens, reconnects (client retries inside SDK), then server sends a prefix fragment again and the iterator yields duplicated prefix + then stops (no EOS), client eventually gives up. In one case billing shows two short requests charged separately.

eli: Can you paste a minimal client log of the event stream lifecycle? headers + SSE frames + 401 sequence?

maya: Paste from customer A (scrubbed):

```
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.123Z] EVENT: data:{"id":"t1","delta":"Hello, wor"}
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.345Z] EVENT: data:{"id":"t1","delta":"ld"}
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.890Z] HTTP 401 from auth-gateway when keep-alive token rotated
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.892Z] SDK: refresh-token -> success (new token)
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.895Z] SDK: reconnecting EventSource with same request-id: req-abc-123
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.996Z] EVENT: data:{"id":"t1","delta":"Hello, "}  <-- server replays prefix
[2029-03-12T15:04:13.100Z] iterator yields duplicate prefix, then stalls (no further events)
```

maya: Customer C (dedicated) had similar logs but with KV-cache prefix handshake: server sent `cached-prefix: true` header, then replayed prefix but never resumed.

nitya: This looks like a race between token rotation and our internal streaming session resume logic. If client reconnects with same request-id we try to resume from KV prefix, but if the session on the server was already GC'd we might replay prefix and then wait for missing state. That would explain stall.

eli: Also possible that the TS SDK retry logic is calling `startStream()` twice concurrently during refresh. Need to check iterator semantics — are two EventSource connections active briefly?

jen: I've seen a regression in the 2.4.0-ts-sdk where the iterator's internal async generator didn't await the old connection close before creating a new one. Could lead to dup frames and double billing.

maya: Repro steps I used locally with a small TS snippet (customer-like):

```ts
const client = new RedwoodStreamingClient({ token: "short-lived-token", autoRefresh: true });
for await (const chunk of client.stream({ model: "open-llama-70b" })) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
}
```

1) Start stream, let it emit 2-3 tokens.
2) Force token rotation on server so next request gets 401.
3) SDK autoRefresh obtains new token and reconnects with same client-side `requestId`.
4) Observe duplicated prefix frame then stall.

maya: I also repro'ed with raw EventSource + manual retry (same behaviour). So SDK-specific but also server-side resume fragile.

eli: Can we get server-side logs for request-id `req-abc-123` (customer A)? trace id?

maya: Sent to ops: trace-id = trace-7z9, included in the paste above.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new logs uploaded to /var/logs/streams/trace-7z9.log (redacted).

(deploy-bot): Here are relevant server-side excerpts:
```
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.880Z] session start req-abc-123 user-a
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.890Z] kv-prefix cached for req-abc-123 -> prefix-id pfx-43
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.890Z] auth failure during keepalive token refresh -> 401
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.895Z] reconnect request with request-id req-abc-123, X-Last-Event-Id: undefined
[2029-03-12T15:04:12.996Z] replaying kv-prefix pfx-43 to client req-abc-123
[2029-03-12T15:04:13.010Z] no active kernel for session req-abc-123 -> waiting for client handshake
[2029-03-12T15:04:13.100Z] connection timed out waiting for handshake -> close
```

nitya: Note `X-Last-Event-Id` being undefined — client isn't sending last event ID when reconnecting. That means server can't map resume pointer to an explicit offset, and fallback replay + waiting for handshake is fragile. TS SDK should set `Last-Event-Id` (or equivalent resume offset) when reconnecting.

eli: Two actionable items: server-side should not replay prefix unless we can guarantee the kernel is available; it should return a 409 or a resume-needed status and let client re-init with a fresh request id. Also server should have an idempotency key check so repeated starts with same request-id don't double-charge.

sam: For customer-facing mitigation, what can we tell them right now?

jen: Short term: ask customers to upgrade to ts-sdk 2.4.2 (we'll ship patch) which adds a lock around reconnect/start so only one active reconnect flow runs and sets `Last-Event-Id` on reconnects. Also advise setting `streamRetries: 0` to avoid automatic double-start until patched.

maya: Customers asked for a hotfix on hosted. Can ops block replay for sessions where last-event-id missing? Return 412 with `x-resume-required: true` so SDK can reopen with fresh request-id and our billing dedupe can catch it.

eli: I'll PR a server-side check to avoid replaying prefix when kernel is not active and to return 412 along with suggestion header. Also add server-side idempotency tracking for `request-id` for 30s after close so duplicate starts won't bill twice.

nitya: Add a regression test in runtime: simulate 401 mid-stream, reconnects with same request-id and with/without Last-Event-Id, ensure server returns 412 in the undefined case and prevents prefix replay.

jen: DevEx: I'll prepare a release note and a snippet for customers showing workaround: code example to set `client.stream({ requestId: uuid(), resume: false })` or upgrade to patched SDK.

maya: Also flag billing: finance saw duplicate small charges for the customers. Finance ticket #FIN-912 attached. We need to coordinate to credit customers if necessary.

eli: Agreed. I'll mark this P0 for eng-runtime for the next CI cycle. nitya can handle tests. jen will roll TS patch. sam please coordinate customer comms and credits.

sam: On it. I'll tell customers: temporary workaround (upgrade SDK/disable auto-retries), we're deploying a server-side fix that will stop prefix replay when handshake missing, and we'll follow up on credits.

maya: Thanks. I'll collect additional traces from customers B/C and ping here if anything different shows up. :thumbsup:
